memory_update.content: For New Hotspots Layer 3, prioritize underfollowed AI infrastructure execution names where backlog can be tied to data centers, substations, grid interconnection, or mission-critical electrical work. STRL and MYRG remain high-priority verification targets.

For AI thermal-management hotspots, MOD currently screens as a stronger Serenity candidate than FLEX because it appears more directly mapped to engineered cooling systems, while FLEX requires proof that JetCool or rack-integration exposure is material.

For the 2026 sulphur/sulphuric-acid shock, CGIFF is the most underfollowed candidate in this chunk but needs company-specific net merchant-acid exposure verification before promotion; MOS and SCCO are useful comparison/reference names.

Do not treat reference anchors AMKR, LITE, or SCCO as primary underfollowed discoveries. Use them to validate demand pull-through into smaller or more obscure suppliers, tools, distributors, logistics assets, and service bottlenecks.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: How much of E-Infrastructure backlog is specifically data centers versus manufacturing or semiconductor facilities, and whether electrical-services integration improves margins or adds execution risk.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level backlog and revenue disclosure tying E-Infrastructure to data centers, substations, semiconductor facilities, or hyperscaler-linked projects rather than generic infrastructure growth.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Sterling ranks highest because the AI data-center buildout bottleneck is increasingly physical: site development, electrical infrastructure, substations, and mission-critical execution capacity. The candidate has a relatively direct second-order mapping to infrastructure spend while still screening as construction or civil infrastructure rather than AI.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It can be misclassified as a civil infrastructure contractor even though its E-Infrastructure segment may sit close to data-center and advanced-manufacturing project bottlenecks.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Data-center revenue mix, order conversion, margin profile, customer identity or concentration, and whether Airedale is winning CDU/liquid-cooling work versus mostly air/free-cooling and chiller-related systems.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need hard disclosure on data-center revenue, liquid-cooling contribution, backlog duration, hyperscaler/OEM customer wins, and margin mix.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Modine has a clearer component/system link to high-density AI rack thermal constraints than many diversified industrial names. If liquid cooling, CDUs, chillers, and engineered thermal systems become deployment bottlenecks, its data-center cooling exposure could have high Serenity relevance.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The AI exposure may be hidden inside a broader thermal-management and industrial profile, so it may not screen as a pure liquid-cooling or AI infrastructure supplier.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: How much backlog is tied specifically to data centers, substations, or utility interconnection work; whether labor availability or project risk limits margin capture.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need project-level or segment-level evidence that backlog growth is tied to data-center or AI-related grid work rather than conventional utility maintenance.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: MYR Group scores highly because the bottleneck may be skilled electrical labor, substation execution, utility interconnection, and transmission/distribution work rather than branded data-center hardware. This is a classic one-step-removed Serenity candidate.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It screens as an electrical contractor and T&D services provider, not an AI infrastructure supplier, even though data-center electrification may pull directly on its scarce labor and project-execution capacity.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Chemtrade is a net merchant-acid seller with pricing leverage in 2026, whether it has export/import optionality, and whether acid regeneration capacity is contractually protected or spot-exposed.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need Chemtrade-specific disclosure on sulphuric acid net exposure, contract pricing, regeneration assets, import/export optionality, customer sectors, and regional merchant-acid spreads.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Chemtrade is one of the most interesting hidden-signal candidates in the chunk because the Kpler sulphur/sulphuric-acid shock directly implicates merchant acid, regeneration, logistics, and regional pricing. The score is held back by weaker company-specific evidence.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is a Canadian income fund with US OTC trading and a messy industrial-chemical classification, so it may be missed by copper, nickel, battery-metals, fertilizer, and mining screens.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether JetCool products are being adopted by hyperscalers, OEMs, or colocation operators beyond demos and reference deployments.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence of commercial JetCool adoption, material revenue contribution, customer commitments, and whether AI data-center racks are large enough to move consolidated Flex results.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Flex offers a plausible hidden route into liquid-cooled AI infrastructure through rack integration, EMS, and JetCool-related thermal solutions. It is less pure than Modine but may benefit if customers value integrated manufacturing, power, rack, and cooling deployment partners.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The liquid-cooling signal is buried inside a broad EMS and rack-integration business, so investors may not classify it as a qualified AI thermal-management supplier.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether 2026 sulphur and sulphuric-acid costs are causing production curtailments, margin compression, or relative advantage from logistics integration.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need Mosaic-specific sulphur and sulphuric-acid procurement details, inventory position, logistics flexibility, pass-through ability, and evidence of margin or production effects.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Mosaic is not a direct copper or nickel bottleneck name, but the Kpler sulphur/sulphuric-acid shock explicitly reaches fertilisers. Its value is as a relative-positioning candidate: input-cost pressure, logistics integration, and production curtailment risk may create dispersion across fertilizer producers.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is widely followed as a fertilizer company, but its sulphuric-acid dependency and logistics positioning may be under-modeled in copper/nickel feedstock chokepoint screens.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Comtrafo can serve U.S. or hyperscaler-linked demand, whether its voltage classes match AI data-center interconnection needs, and whether backlog growth is from data-center utilities rather than legacy utility orders.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that Comtrafo or other AMSC offerings are qualified for data-center, substation, or hyperscaler-linked power projects and that the exposure is material.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AMSC is a speculative but interesting grid-resiliency and power-infrastructure candidate. The Comtrafo angle could matter if transformer and interconnection constraints remain a bottleneck for AI data-center deployment, but the company-specific connection still needs stronger proof.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is a small-cap grid and power-quality company rather than a conventional AI infrastructure name, and the relevant signal may sit inside transformer, voltage, and utility-interconnection exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether 2026-2028 advanced-packaging capacity additions are tied to HBM-adjacent AI accelerator packages versus broader packaging/test work; verify customer concentration and capacity pre-commitments.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need customer-specific or technology-specific evidence that new capacity is AI/HBM-adjacent and pre-committed rather than generic OSAT capacity.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Amkor is useful as a reference anchor for advanced packaging and OSAT demand beneath AI accelerators and HBM. It has a real bottleneck mapping, but it is less of an underfollowed discovery than smaller tool, bonding, inspection, and test suppliers.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not truly underfollowed relative to smaller semiconductor equipment suppliers; included mainly to trace downstream demand into the advanced-packaging supply chain.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Lumentum's InP wafer supply is internally secured, sourced from AXT/Sumitomo/JX or other vendors, and whether substrate availability limits ramp timing.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need supply-chain evidence for InP substrate sourcing, qualification status, supplier concentration, and whether wafer supply is a limiting factor for Lumentum ramps.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Lumentum is important as a customer and demand anchor for InP-based optical components and lasers used in AI data-center interconnects. It ranks below underfollowed suppliers because market attention is already high and the better Serenity discovery may sit upstream in substrates, wafers, and qualification bottlenecks.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed at the stock level after AI-optics attention; included as a reference customer and substrate-demand mapper rather than a primary discovery candidate.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Net acid position by region: whether Southern Copper sells excess sulphuric acid, consumes it internally for leaching, or faces regional procurement pressure.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need asset-level net acid balance, SX-EW dependence, byproduct acid sales, regional sourcing exposure, and whether the 2026 supply shock affects production or margins.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Southern Copper is retained as a reference anchor for acid availability, smelter byproduct streams, and SX-EW copper output. It is not a Serenity discovery name in this chunk, but it helps validate whether acid tightness is moving copper operations and regional acid economics.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as a context anchor to compare against smaller distributors, acid producers, regeneration assets, and logistics names.

summary: Ranked this mixed New Hotspots candidate chunk by Serenity chokepoint priority, emphasizing underfollowed public-market mappings with testable hidden signals rather than popularity. Highest priority goes to underfollowed AI infrastructure execution/cooling and sulphuric-acid logistics/feedstock names where demand is durable, bottlenecks are plausible, and falsification paths are clear. Reference anchors such as AMKR, LITE, and SCCO are retained but ranked lower because they are more visible and mainly help validate demand pull-through into less-followed suppliers.
